html:
The Xakriabá are an Indigenous people of northern Minas Gerais, in southeastern Brazil, near São João das Missões. About 9,200 lived there in 2010.

They are a Jê people, related to the Akwẽ (Xerente and Xavante), who once lived further north in the Tocantins River region. Settlers and missions pushed them onto a small part of their land in the 1700s, and they now speak Portuguese. In 1987 their leader Rosalino Gomes was murdered in a land dispute, and their territory was officially recognised in the years that followed. Other peoples of the region include the Maxakalí and the Pataxó.
sum: The Xakriabá are an Indigenous people of northern Minas Gerais, in southeastern Brazil, near São João das Missões. About 9,200 lived there in 2010.
